subject: Waste Hauler Bundled Service Ordinance
overview: The subcommittee reviewed a draft merging proposed waste hauler regulations with existing solid waste ordinances to modernize collection practices and enforcement. Key decisions focused on requiring private haulers to provide bundled trash and recycling services and updating the permitting authority of the Board of Health.

items.title: Proposed Updates to Chapter 70 Solid Waste Ordinance
items.summary: The subcommittee reviewed a working draft that incorporates a new waste hauler proposal into the existing city code to simplify outdated regulations.

items.title: Effective Date and Contract Alignment
items.summary: The subcommittee discussed setting the ordinance's effective date to July 1, 2024, to align with the city's new waste contract and provide businesses a transition period for bundled services.

items.title: Collection Authority and Prescription
items.summary: The subcommittee simplified Section 70-72 to grant the DPW Commissioner authority over collection requirements, removing outdated and overly prescriptive sorting rules for specific materials.

items.title: Permit Requirements and Tonnage Reporting
items.summary: Updates to the hauler permit process were discussed, including new requirements for reporting annual tonnage of waste and recyclables to aid in city greenhouse gas reporting.

items.title: Bundled Service and Space Constraints
items.summary: The subcommittee addressed the requirement for haulers to provide combined trash and recycling services, acknowledging that city staff must work with small businesses on space constraints for extra containers.

items.title: Construction and Temporary Dumpster Exemptions
items.summary: The draft was updated to explicitly exempt construction debris and temporary dumpsters from the bundling requirements of the ordinance.

items.title: Enforcement, Penalties, and Appeals
items.summary: The subcommittee established a tiered fine schedule for violations and designated the Board of Health to promulgate regulations for the citation appeal process.

items.title: Referral of Article I to Code Enforcement
items.summary: The subcommittee referred Article I, which deals with routine debris and sidewalk obstructions, to the Code Enforcement Commissioner for review and modernization of its language.

items.title: Adoption of Draft and Next Steps
items.summary: The subcommittee moved to produce a clean, non-redline draft for final review by relevant department heads and legal counsel before further action.
